summary: Security audit of layout/UX change set d5bb5e3..HEAD (20 files, no api/db/auth changes). The one new untrusted-input surface, parseDuelInvite(), is a correct fail-closed allow-list parser; its only caller navigates from the parsed id, not the raw paste. ClimbBoard reads the existing /api/dashboard with the viewer's own token (no IDOR), fully narrows the response at runtime, and degrades safely. No secrets, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/eval, no untrusted redirects/hrefs, no dependency changes. No critical or high findings.
goal: Audit the branch change set for auth, secrets, injection, open redirects, untrusted input, and dependency issues per .claude/rules/security.md and context/trust.md.

findings.issue: parseDuelInvite() reviewed against all four adversarial vectors: bare id is strict allow-list [A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,64}; protocol-relative //host rejected (line 56); javascript:/data: rejected by http(s)-only check (line 67); cross-origin absolute URLs rejected by url.origin !== expectedOrigin (line 68); fails CLOSED when origin is opaque/unresolvable (appOrigin returns null -> expectedOrigin null -> all absolute URLs rejected). Returns null, never a substituted default. Confirmed HARDENED.
findings.reproduction: Paste `javascript:alert(1)`, `//evil.com/duel/abcdef`, `https://evil.com/duel/abcdef`, or `data:...` into /duel invite box -> all yield null -> inline error, no navigation.

findings.issue: Sole caller handleOpenInvite builds the navigation target as `/duel/${duelId}` from the PARSED id (matched by DUEL_ID/DUEL_PATH regex), never from the raw pasted string. No open-redirect or javascript:-navigation path reachable. Other router.push sites (162,164,185,211,248) use own-API response ids, not the invite input. Share link at :162 uses window.location.origin (browser-trusted) + own-API existingId, carries no secret.

Reads existing GET /api/dashboard via authedFetch with the VIEWER'S OWN token - no user-controlled id in the request, so no IDOR/cross-user leak. Response is runtime-narrowed by toViewerRecord (typeof/Number.isFinite checks), not cast, matching conventions.md. Failure (non-ok, throw, or unparseable) degrades to status 'unavailable' -> CTA-only panel. Client-side search filters already-rendered rows via React text interpolation (no XSS). No new endpoint introduced.

searchParams.get('mode') is allow-listed to 'chips'|'tournaments' and otherwise resolves to 'free'. This defaults rather than returning null, but it is cosmetic UI tab state (not a write path or trust boundary), 'free' is the LEAST-privileged value, and actual paid-duel gating is enforced server-side. The reject-never-default rule targets write/lookup paths; not a violation here. No injection - value only selects a UI branch, never reaches a DOM/URL sink.
findings.reproduction: Visit /duel?mode=<payload> -> falls to 'free' tab; value never reflected into markup or a request.

learnings.insight: Security audit of d5bb5e3..HEAD clean: 0 critical/0 high. Only new untrusted-input surface is parseDuelInvite (fail-closed allow-list, caller navigates from parsed id). ClimbBoard uses own-token /api/dashboard read with runtime narrowing + safe degradation. No secrets, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/eval, no untrusted redirects, no dependency/lockfile changes, no api/db/auth changes.
learnings.action: Proceed to qa-acceptance; no security loop-back required.

learnings.insight: parseDuelInvite is the reference pattern for accepting a pasted link: allow-list regex for the bare id, reject protocol-relative (//), reject non-http(s) schemes, reject cross-origin by comparing url.origin to a browser/config-derived expectedOrigin, and fail CLOSED (return null) when origin is opaque. The caller MUST rebuild the target from the returned id, never the raw input.
learnings.action: Reuse this shape for any future pasted-URL/user-supplied-link feature; never pass a raw pasted string to router.push/fetch.
